unanticipated_findings: Unbounded SQLite connection / file-descriptor leak under the bundled server. DeliveryStore opens one connection per thread lazily (src/webhookd/store.py:84-105) and appends every one to self._connections (store.py:104), which is only ever emptied by close() (store.py:112-121). ThreadingWSGIServer (src/webhookd/server.py:34-40) uses ThreadingMixIn with daemon_threads=True, i.e. a new thread per connection, so every inbound HTTP connection permanently adds a SQLite connection object and its file descriptors. Reproduced against `webhookd serve --port 8123`: fds on the server pid went 4 (idle, before any traffic reached the store) -> 105 after ~46 requests -> 225 after 60 more, i.e. ~2 fds leaked per request and never reclaimed; `ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd | grep -c sqlite3` gave 221 while `ls /proc/<pid>/task | wc -l` was 5 (the request threads had all exited — only their connections remained). At a default `ulimit -n` of 1024 the process would start failing to open files after roughly 400-500 deliveries. Not covered by any test.

The bundled server has no read timeout, so a client can pin a request thread indefinitely with a declared-but-unsent body. src/webhookd/app.py:204 does `stream.read(length)` with no deadline; ThreadingWSGIServer sets `timeout = 30` (server.py:40) but that attribute governs socketserver's handle_request() polling, not per-connection reads, and WSGIRequestHandler.timeout is never set. Reproduced: opened a raw socket to the server and sent `POST /hooks/acme HTTP/1.1 ... Content-Length: 5000` followed by only 2 bytes of body — no response after 20s ('NO RESPONSE after 20.1s'), whereas a well-formed request answers in ~1ms. With daemon_threads=True and no thread cap, N such connections consume N threads. The comment at server.py:39 explicitly claims 'A slow or hung sender must not be able to occupy a connection forever', which the code does not achieve.

README quickstart inconsistency around --port. README.md:31 offers `webhookd serve --port 8123` when 8080 is taken, but `webhookd send` has no --port flag and derives its URL from [server] in the config (src/webhookd/cli.py:112), and the README never mentions the `--url` flag that would bridge the two. I hit this: with the server on 8123, `webhookd send acme -d '{"order": 7}'` printed `404` (it posted to :8080, where an unrelated process was listening) with no hint as to why. Following the default-port path in the README works fully; only the documented fallback branch is broken.

Deduplication silently degrades to content hashing when the delivery-id header is absent. src/webhookd/app.py:227-244: if `delivery_id_header` yields no value and `require_delivery_id` is false (the default, config.py:77), the key becomes sha256(raw_timestamp + body). A sender that re-signs each retry with a fresh timestamp therefore produces a different key per retry and the handler runs once per attempt — the exact duplicate-work case the service exists to prevent. The behaviour is documented (README.md:130-134) and `require_delivery_id = true` opts out, but the insecure-by-omission default means a misconfigured sender loses the guarantee without any warning at startup or in `webhookd check`.
